items.headline: Six TIL therapy companies to watch out for
items.preview: A look at six promising companies developing tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapies.
items.article:
Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy is a type of cell therapy that utilizes a patient’s own immune cells to combat cancer. Currently, Iovance Biotherapeutics' Amtagvi is the only approved TIL therapy for melanoma in the U.S. and Australia. Various biotechs are now developing TIL therapies in clinical trials, aiming to treat different solid tumors.
Why this matters: With the potential to harness the body’s immune response against cancer, TIL therapies represent a significant advancement in cancer treatment, particularly for patients with solid tumors that are traditionally difficult to treat. Companies like Iovance, Curacell, and Obsidian Therapeutics are leading the charge in this innovative field.

items.headline: From confidence to capital: Positioning biotech for the next growth cycle
items.preview: Biotech confidence is rising, with increased deal-making and strategic partnerships.
items.article:
2026 has seen a resurgence of confidence in biotech, highlighted by optimistic discussions at major conferences like DIA China and BIO International Convention. The first quarter of this year recorded the highest number of deals since 2023, indicating a robust market for partnerships and outlicensing deals as companies prepare for the impending patent cliff.
Why this matters: As biotechs position themselves for growth, understanding market dynamics and investor readiness becomes crucial for capitalizing on new opportunities and ensuring sustainable development in the sector.

items.headline: Fast-track trial approval: a way to jump the EU queue?
items.preview: New accelerated pathways in the EU aim to streamline clinical trial approvals.
items.article:
The EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) was launched to centralize clinical trial applications but has inadvertently increased approval timelines. In response, several EU nations are introducing accelerated pathways for trials, particularly for innovative therapies. For instance, France aims for a 14-day approval for clean dossiers, significantly faster than the standard route.
Why this matters: These new fast-track options could enhance the speed of bringing innovative therapies to market, providing a competitive edge for biotechs navigating the complex regulatory landscape in Europe.

items.headline: Mouse models and CRO selection critical to de-risking neurology drug development
items.preview: Choosing the right mouse models and CROs is vital for successful CNS drug development.
items.article:
As the first disease-modifying Alzheimer’s therapy, Leqembi's approval marks a significant milestone, yet CNS drug development remains fraught with challenges. GemPharmatech emphasizes the importance of selecting appropriate mouse models to better understand disease mechanisms and therapeutic efficacy. Their advanced models aim to replicate human disease pathology more accurately.
Why this matters: Effective preclinical models are essential for reducing the risk of failure in clinical trials, particularly in the complex field of neurology, where traditional models often fall short.

items.headline: Where next for structural bioinformatics?
items.preview: Exploring the future directions of structural bioinformatics in light of recent advancements.
items.article:
The advent of AlphaFold has revolutionized structural biology, yet challenges remain in understanding protein folding and function. Structural bioinformatics is evolving, focusing on predictive models and biomolecule design. However, there is a call for the field to shift from mere prediction to deeper biological understanding and informatics.
Why this matters: As structural bioinformatics continues to advance, it is crucial for researchers to leverage these tools not just for predictions but to gain insights that can drive biological discoveries and therapeutic innovations.
